title: ICT and access

blocks.heading: ICT and access
blocks.text: ICT can support learning materials, communication and flexible access, but requires usable devices, power, connectivity, skills and suitable content. It may widen opportunities or deepen a digital gap. Learning gains need evidence; distributing devices alone does not establish teaching or access.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: An invented learning centre supplies offline audio lessons with charged players and a tutor trained to support their use. The equipment can widen access to materials, but lessons still need to suit the curriculum and learners’ language needs. A device count is an input measure; participation and learning provide better evidence of whether the arrangement is useful.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
